g.text: Owners and commissioners across six U.S. sports leagues made $47.0 million in federal political contributions over the 2016,

text.style: font-size: 11.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #52514e

g.text: 2018 and 2020 election cycles, per FiveThirtyEight's donation tracker — 73% of the money went to Republican candidates and

text.style: font-size: 11.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #52514e

g.text: PACs, and only one league's ownership tilted blue: the WNBA's.

g.text: parties and PACs by 158 owners and commissioners in MLB, NBA, NFL, NHL, WNBA and NASCAR, 2016 / 2018 / 2020 cycles, with each recipient's party lean as classified by

g.text: FiveThirtyEight. “Mostly Republican / mostly Democratic” bipartisan committees are folded into the respective party; $0.85M to committees with no party listed (largely Jerry

text.style: font-size: 7.3px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: Reinsdorf's $0.8M to three PACs) is counted as gray alongside bipartisan giving. League shares double-count owners who hold teams in more than one league.
